network_thesis.headline: Yassir × Navier — the Maghreb super-app, now with a water tier
network_thesis.body: Yassir already sells the hardest coordination layer in the Maghreb: trusted mobility demand, payments, delivery, merchant density, and driver/partner supply. Navier gives that app a premium coastal transport surface in places where road congestion, port geography, tourism transfers, and cross-water shortcuts are visible but not yet owned by any super-app.

network_thesis.how_to_read: Start with the anchor markets below — each opens a full market proposal with corridors, phasing, and unit economics.

partner_context.their_ambition: Yassir is the leading super app for French-speaking Africa and the Maghreb. YC and Google Cloud both describe a platform operating in 45 cities across Algeria, Morocco, and Tunisia, with ride-hailing, last-mile delivery, and financial services as the connective tissue.
partner_context.their_pressure: Ride-hailing density compounds in the cities, but coastal North Africa leaves trips fragmented between taxis, ferries, rail, and informal transfers. The premium-water surface is still unclaimed.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is a branded water tier inside Yassir: app-booked, cashless, captain-operated — starting with short, high-frequency coastal hops and growing into longer strait and inter-city runs as the fleet range extends.
partner_context.algeria_note: Yassir was born in Algiers — and Algiers bay is a natural water city. The home market is a first-class pillar of this network, mapped corridor-for-corridor alongside Morocco, Tunisia, and Senegal.

hero.title: Yassir × Navier — the Maghreb super-app, now with a water tier
hero.subtitle: Four coastal countries, 45 cities, one app. Water is the only transport surface no one owns yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We launch a Yassir-branded premium water tier across the Maghreb's coastal cities and Dakar — Tangier, Casablanca, Agadir and Al Hoceima; Algiers, Oran and Annaba; Tunis, La Goulette, Sidi Bou Said and Djerba; Dakar and the Petite Côte. Yassir owns the customer, the wallet, the captain-partner supply, and the door-to-pier leg; Navier brings the silent hydrofoiling fleet and the operating playbook proven in the Maldives.

why_now: North African cities are building super-app behavior while coastal trips remain slow, cash-heavy, and disconnected from the daily mobility stack. The first partner to connect ride-hail, port pickup, water transfer, and arrival ride in one checkout becomes the default premium layer for coastal trips.

why_navier_now.step_change: The N30 proves short, high-frequency coastal hops today — silent, smooth, and roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional boat. The longer-range Quanta program extends the same network to strait crossings and inter-city legs as it matures, so the proposal has both launch-now routes and a visible roadmap.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Uses existing waterways, marinas, ports, and app dispatch rather than new right-of-way.
why_navier_now.the_moment: North African cities are building super-app behavior while coastal trips remain slow, cash-heavy, and disconnected from the daily mobility stack. The first partner to connect ride-hail, port pickup, water transfer, and arrival ride in one checkout becomes the default premium layer for coastal trips.

multimodal_fit: Yassir can book the whole journey: home pickup → marina/port handoff → Navier water leg → arrival taxi/food/cash/payment touchpoints. This is not a ferry brochure; it is a super-app surface extension.

precedents.what: A live ~100-vessel network in the Maldives moving guests across a $100M water-mobility market.
precedents.why_it_matters: The fleet, the captain model, and the app integration Yassir would launch with are already operating at national scale.

precedents.what: Super-app water tiers are being launched with leading ride-hail platforms across Southeast Asia and the Gulf.
precedents.why_it_matters: The playbook — app-booked water legs beside the car tier — is proven; the Maghreb is the next unclaimed region.

precedents.what: Every corridor shown here is a real pier-to-pier route on the live map, with distances and demand behind it.
precedents.why_it_matters: This is a network you can inspect route by route — not a concept map.

differentiation.headline: Exactness over coverage
differentiation.body: Every corridor on the live map is a real, on-water route between named piers — measured, not hand-drawn. Where a market is still early we say so and show the roadmap, so the map you present internally is the map we can actually launch.

proof_points: YC profile: Yassir operates in 45 cities across Algeria, Morocco, and Tunisia and offers ride-hailing/last-mile delivery/financial services.
Google Cloud customer story repeats the 45-city Algeria/Morocco/Tunisia operating footprint and frames Yassir as a Maghreb super-app.
Official Yassir site foregrounds ride-hailing, food delivery, market, cash, and driver/delivery partner onboarding.
35 corridors mapped across the four countries, each a named pier-to-pier route with distance and demand behind it.
Flagship economics are strong: Tangier Marina Bay ↔ Tarifa models at ~81% margin per vessel; La Goulette ↔ Sidi Bou Said at ~75%.
Dakar ↔ Gorée is already one of West Africa's busiest short crossings — demand exists today; the experience upgrade doesn't.

objections.objection: Yassir is not proven city-by-city on every route.
objections.response: Every market shown is one where Yassir already operates and where the corridors are real, mapped pier-to-pier routes. We launch where the water and the demand are ready today, and grow the map together from there.

objections.objection: Algeria is Yassir's home market — why not include it on the map?
objections.response: Every market shown is one where Yassir already operates and where the corridors are real, mapped pier-to-pier routes. We launch where the water and the demand are ready today, and grow the map together from there.

objections.objection: Some Morocco/Tunisia demand rows are estimated.
objections.response: The economics publish grounded floor separately from estimated upside; the model and proposal expose that separation.

objections.objection: Can N30 do the longer Mediterranean legs?
objections.response: No. The proposal range-gates them to Quanta-LR roadmap or review; long legs are not faked.

objections.objection: Why is Algeria not shown as a Yassir market if Yassir started there?
objections.response: Every market shown is one where Yassir already operates and where the corridors are real, mapped pier-to-pier routes. We launch where the water and the demand are ready today, and grow the map together from there.

markets.label: Morocco — Tangier, Casablanca, Agadir & Al Hoceima
markets.summary: Yassir's strongest water market: the Tangier bay network, the Casablanca–Mohammedia commuter run, Al Hoceima's coves — and the cross-strait flagship to Tarifa behind them.

hero.title: Yassir × Navier — Morocco, the anchor market
hero.subtitle: Dense Atlantic and strait cities, with the network's flagship crossing waiting at Tangier.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Yassir-branded foiling water tier across Morocco's coastal cities — Tangier bay hops, the Casablanca commuter run, Al Hoceima's beach coves and Agadir's surf coast — booked in-app beside the car tier, with the Strait of Gibraltar flagship as the marquee.

partner_context.their_ambition: Morocco is Yassir's biggest expansion surface: the kingdom's coastal cities hold most of its population, its tourism, and its premium demand.
partner_context.their_pressure: Coastal trips are slow and fragmented — bay detours by road, congested corniches, and a tourism market that pays for experience but can't book it in one place.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A premium water tier inside Yassir on Morocco's densest coastal corridors — minutes across Tangier bay instead of a drive around it, with pickup and arrival handled by the app.

markets.why_now: Tangier bay, the Casablanca–Mohammedia corridor, and the Al Hoceima coast all have visible daily demand and no premium water option. And the Strait of Gibraltar — one of the world's most famous crossings — is a 30-minute foiling run from Tangier Marina Bay.
markets.multimodal_fit: Yassir captures the land legs around Navier's water leg.

hero.title: Yassir × Navier — Algeria, the home market
hero.subtitle: The super-app was born in Algiers. The bay it looks out on is the network's most natural water city.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Yassir-branded water tier across Algiers bay — the marina at Sidi Fredj, El Djamila, the eastern beaches at Aïn Taya and Tamentfoust, all connected through the Port d'Alger — with Oran's gulf and Annaba's corniche on the same fleet.

partner_context.their_ambition: Algeria is where Yassir started and where its brand is strongest — the home market deserves the flagship treatment, not an afterthought.
partner_context.their_pressure: Algiers' corniche traffic is severe and the bay's beach towns are minutes away by water but an hour by road; there is no premium mobility option on the water at all.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A premium foiling tier inside Yassir across Algiers bay and the Oran and Annaba waterfronts — the home market's most visible product launch in years.

markets.why_now: Algiers bay is ringed with marinas, beach towns, and a working port — Sidi Fredj, El Djamila, Aïn Taya, Tamentfoust — all minutes apart by water and painfully far by corniche traffic. No one owns this surface. The home team should.

proof_points.claim: Algiers bay is a ready-made water network.
proof_points.evidence: Seven mapped corridors connect the bay's marinas, beaches, and the city port — most under 12 nm, ideal N30 range.
Launching the water tier in Algiers is the strongest possible brand statement for an Algiers-born super-app.
The El Djamila ↔ Port d'Alger corridor models profitably on observed demand — the launch is grounded, not speculative.

markets.the_ask: Make the home market a launch market: one boat proves Algiers bay in a season, and the brand story writes itself.

close.title: The home market deserves the flagship.
close.body: Yassir was born looking at this bay. Put the first foiling tier on it.

markets.why_now: La Goulette to Sidi Bou Said is a 4 nm hop between Tunisia's cruise port and its most photographed village — today it's a taxi through traffic. The bay, the riviera, and Djerba's lagoon are all N30-perfect water with visible daily demand.

growth.anchor_note: LB-254: M_today = transport_spend_pool_yr (demand x fare); the ladder's capture = floor/pool (the capture that actually built the floor: ~0.90 captive / ~0.10 contested / blended). Replaces the legacy floor/0.10 divisor that inflated captive markets ~9x.

_whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
_whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total spend on the whole island journey flowing through the super-app: transport + food + stays + experiences + ads + parcel/logistics. Gross, all merchants. TAM rung is in this unit.
_whose_money_legend.platform_take: The partner's (Grab's) own commission revenue on journey_gmv. Derived line — this is the number that makes a super-app care, not the boat fare.

alpha_density._doc: avg greenfield corridor demand / avg sourced corridor demand. Sourced = cherry-picked best; greenfield thinner.

_census._note: tier1 market-making (island-hop/regional/inter-city/trunk) + tier2 cluster-spokes; Japan/Ryukyu carved out; local intra-hub micro-segments excluded.

greenfield._doc: WIDTH lever. SAM_sourced_only = depth on the sourced corridors (no greenfield). SAM/TAM/network/platform = full addressable network (sourced + greenfield). SOM floor is unaffected (it is the sourced corridors).

revenue_potential.headline: The floor and the prize — every rung traces to grounded, sourced demand.
revenue_potential.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
revenue_potential.anchor_note: $111M/yr premium sea-transfer spend on sourced corridors today — the anchor every rung builds from.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total spend on the whole island journey flowing through the super-app: transport + food + stays + experiences + ads + parcel/logistics. Gross, all merchants. TAM rung is in this unit.
whose_money_legend.platform_take: The partner's (Grab's) own commission revenue on journey_gmv. Derived line — this is the number that makes a super-app care, not the boat fare.

revenue_potential.cite_rule: Cite MID. 'High' stacks every optimistic assumption — ceiling, not headline.

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.headline: Lens shift: Navier captured share → total inducible marine-transfer wallet
ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marine transfer → total journey wallet (food, stays, experiences, in-app ads)
ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.

ladder_transitions.headline: Yassir platform take on Navier-carried journeys
ladder_transitions.basis: Platform-take step. Platform commission applied to the journey GMV routed through the Navier network (Navier-captured subset, not the full induced market).
